newsitem.title: USA: Vivus gets FDA OK for MUSE impotence drug.
newsitem.headline: Vivus gets FDA OK for MUSE impotence drug.

text.p: VIVUS Inc said Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved the use of MUSE in treating impotence.

MUSE is a single-use disposable applicator containing alprostadil, a synthetic version of the naturally-occurring vasodilator prostaglandin E1. Alprostadil got FDA marketing clearance last year as an injection, the company said.
VIVUS, which was founded in 1991 to develop treatments for impotence, said it will seek to begin marketing MUSE after it gets final FDA marketing clearance.
Final FDA marketing clearance is subject to labeling requirements and agreement that the VIVUS manufacturing facility, methods and controls comply with FDA requirements, the company said.
